reasons: A limitation-of-liability section exists (Section 7) but contains only a consequential-damages exclusion with no monetary cap, so neither party's direct liability is capped; that fails the fallback (mutual 12-month cap with carve-outs), making 'deviation' an appropriate classification for a partially-present clause.

The redline is additive and minimal: it leaves the existing exclusion sentence untouched and inserts a single new paragraph (b) establishing a mutual aggregate cap plus an Excluded Claims definition, consistent with the redline guidance to edit rather than rewrite the section.

The cap tracks the preferred position (greater of twelve months' amounts and USD 1,000,000) and carries the full preferred carve-out set (confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) outside the cap.

Substituting 'amounts paid or payable between the Parties' for 'fees paid by Customer' is a justified adaptation to the revenue-share model in Section 5 (Vendor pays Customer), avoiding an illusory cap; the USD 1,000,000 floor keeps the cap meaningful in any event.
Carving Section 5 revenue-share amounts out of the limitation mirrors the playbook's 'payment obligations are not damages' principle and is directionally correct for us as Customer.

The comment is accurate, concise, states the playbook position, flags that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap, and offers a fees-only twelve-month fallback; deterministic checks all pass.
